AT/Bregenz.note: the city groundwater; the Fluh springs supply 13.8 dH

AT/Feldkirch.note: spring water at 7-9 dH, Frastanzerried groundwater at 15-17; the blend at a tap depends on the day's mix

AT/Graz.note: midpoint of the published 15-17 dH range, which straddles the boundary between Austrian hardness levels II and III

AT/Innsbruck.note: the main city zone; outlying zones run from 1.5 dH at Amras to 21.2 dH in Oberes Hötting West

AT/Klagenfurt.note: midpoint of the published 17-20 dH range

AT/Kufstein.note: Hofinger spring and the Fuerhoelzl deep well; hardness directories claim far higher figures than the utility itself publishes

AT/Leoben.note: the analysis figure; the supply area as a whole runs 9-14 dH

AT/Linz.note: median of eleven supply zones measuring 16.2-21.3 dH; all eleven fall in hardness level III

AT/Salzburg.note: about 10 dH across 90 percent of the supply area; the Tiefenbach spring zones on the edge of the city run 17-18 dH

AT/Steyr.note: wells in the Dietach and Tinsting groundwater fields

AT/Vienna.note: 6-12 dH across most of the city; districts 2, 3, 11, 20, 21 and 22 take groundwater as well and run 6-20 dH

AT/Villach.note: the Union spring, which supplies the city proper; Landskron runs 14.0-16.0 dH and Mittewald 12.3 dH

AT/Wels.note: the Messegelände zone; the other zones in the city measure 10.3-11.6 dH

AT/Wiener Neustadt.note: median of the four distribution areas, which measure 15.2-19.9 dH

CH/Basel.note: midpoint of the published 16-19 f range

CH/Bern.note: midpoint of the published 20-30 f range across the three catchments in the Emmental, at Kiesen and in the Aare valley

CH/Geneva.note: lake water, which supplies most of the city; the networks fed from the Genevois aquifer run 18.3-21.2 f

CH/Lausanne.note: water from Lake Geneva is soft at 14 f, the Thierrens springs fairly hard at 28 f; which reservoir feeds a street decides the figure

CH/Lucerne.note: lake water 11 f, spring water 13-20 f, groundwater about 28 f; which of them reaches a district decides the figure

CH/Lugano.note: average of 123 measurements across the integrated network, which spans 2-29 f; the central districts measure 10-12 f

CH/Neuchatel.note: average of 49 measurements; the network spans 14.5-40.4 f, so a single figure hides a lot

CH/Riehen.note: supplied through the cantonal IWB network at 18.9 f; the village also keeps its own small spring network from the Au and Moostal valleys

CH/Sion.note: the Sion Plaine zone, which covers the town centre; the Coteau rive droite zone measures 21.6 f and the Coteau rive gauche 29.3 f

CH/St. Gallen.note: the city takes all of its water from Lake Constance, which is why the span is so narrow

CH/Winterthur.note: average of 34 measurements; outlying districts on spring water run about 36 f

DE/Aachen.note: 3.4-4.0 dH from Roetgen, 9.7-10.9 dH from Binsfeldhammer; STAWAG states hard water does not occur in its area

DE/Augsburg.note: published range 13.5-13.9 dH across the whole supply area

DE/Bielefeld.note: eleven waterworks from 4.3 dH at the softest to 17.1 dH at the hardest; the utility lists each with its figure

DE/Bonn.note: midpoint of the published 4.4-7.0 dH range

DE/Braunschweig.note: exactly on the soft/medium boundary; the supply mix changed in February 2024, when Harz reservoir water was joined by groundwater from Börßum

DE/Bremen.note: Bremen-Stadt zone, 6.3 dH; other zones run to 13.5 dH

DE/Bremerhaven.note: three works, all in the medium band: Langen 9.0 dH, Bexhövede 9.5, Leherheide 11.4

DE/Chemnitz.note: the whole supply area sits in the soft band; the utility notes descaling agents are unnecessary

DE/Cologne.note: 18.1 dH left of the Rhine, 15.6 dH right

DE/Cottbus.note: computed from the accredited report's calcium (87.5 mg/L) and magnesium (11.5 mg/L), which is the definition of total hardness; the sample is the Sachsendorf zone, and the city's other zones differ

DE/Dresden.note: the Coschütz works supplies zone 1 with soft water at 5.6 dH; the mixing zones with Hosterwitz and Tolkewitz Elbe water run to 12.3 dH

DE/Duisburg.note: midpoint of four supply areas, 11-18 dH

DE/Erfurt.note: most of the city gets mixed water at 12-14 dH; the eastern districts get soft long-distance water at about 3.1 dH, and the utility looks the figure up per street

DE/Erlangen.note: own works at 9.8-12.9 dH in the medium band; purchased N-ERGIE and WFW water crosses into hard

DE/Frankfurt am Main.note: the city draws on several Hessenwasser sources, mixed differently per district; Mainova's site looks the figure up per address

DE/Freiburg im Breisgau.note: four supply areas, 2.3-12.7 dH; soft in three of them

DE/Gelsenkirchen.note: the Haltern works supplies most of the city; Feldmark, Neustadt, Rotthausen and Ückendorf get softer Essen water at 7.7 dH

DE/Göttingen.note: published as 6.6-7.3 dH; the utility notes that softening salts for household machines are unnecessary

DE/Halle (Saale).note: from the Beesen works; water leaving the Wienrode works measures 4.1 dH

DE/Hamburg.note: 5.1-18.3 dH across waterworks, spans three bands; no single city figure is published

DE/Heidelberg.note: two soft zones at 2.7-6.6 dH and two hard zones at 17.5-21.1 dH; a single figure would mislead

DE/Heilbronn.note: four hardness areas at 9, 10, 14 and 14-18 dH; the utility publishes a street directory naming each one

DE/Hildesheim.note: Harz reservoir water; the softest city figure in this collection

DE/Jena.note: the Burgau works serves much of the city with hard water at 18.5 dH, Drackendorf at 14.8; streets on Thuringian long-distance water get 3.2 dH, and the utility lists every street

DE/Kaiserslautern.note: three waterworks, all soft: Mölschbach 4.2 dH, Barbarossastraße 4.5, Rote Hohl 5.1

DE/Kassel.note: fourteen storage reservoirs serve the city: around 11 dH in the centre, up to about 15 dH in Harleshausen and Kirchditmold; the utility looks the figure up per address

DE/Koblenz.published_value: only a hardness band per district (mittel or hart)
DE/Koblenz.note: VWM's district map: Altstadt, Luetzel, Neuendorf, Kesselheim, Wallersheim, Metternich, Guels and Rauental are hart; Karthause, Oberwerth, Ehrenbreitstein, Pfaffendorf, Arenberg and most right-bank districts mittel; the address lookup on the evm site answers per street

DE/Krefeld.note: the raw groundwater is centrally softened to 13 dH before distribution

DE/Leipzig.note: two thirds of the city drinks hard water from the Naunhof, Canitz and Thallwitz works at up to 18.5 dH; the remaining third arrives at medium hardness from the Elbaue-Ostharz long-distance supply

DE/Leverkusen.published_value: no citywide figure; both supply areas classed weich
DE/Leverkusen.note: Dhünn reservoir water and Rheindorf groundwater; EVL classes both supply areas weich and publishes no citywide figure

DE/Ludwigshafen am Rhein.note: the Parkinsel works supplies the inner districts at 14.5 dH, Maudach-Oggersheim the north and west at 10.8

DE/Lübeck.note: the utility's own quality sheet gives 11.1-16.3 dH and classes the water as hart

DE/Magdeburg.note: all of it from the Colbitz works in the Colbitz-Letzlinger Heide; the figure sits so close to the 14.0 boundary that SWM's own pages label it hart in one place and mittel in another

DE/Mainz.note: three waterworks: Hof Schönau at 12.6 dH, Eich at 19.3 dH and Petersaue at 25.1 dH; which one supplies a street decides the figure

DE/Munster.note: midpoint of four waterworks; softening at Hornheide began August 2026, so this will fall

DE/Mönchengladbach.note: NEW puts the whole city in the medium band; six waterworks feed it, and which one serves a street is not published

DE/Mülheim (Ruhr).note: median of the Mülheim-Styrum works' 2025 data; Mintard is served separately

DE/Nuremberg.note: midpoint of four supply networks, 9.5-13.6 dH

DE/Oberhausen.note: two zones split along the A42: the south drinks Mülheim-Styrum water at a median of 8.0 dH (soft), the north Dorsten-Holsterhausen water at 13.5 dH (medium)

DE/Offenbach.source: Zweckverband Wasserversorgung Stadt und Kreis Offenbach (ZWO)
DE/Offenbach.note: the published span for the city network, all of it in the medium band

DE/Oldenburg.note: three waterworks: Sandkrug is soft at 6.6 dH, Donnerschwee 11.8 and Alexanderfeld 12 sit in the medium band; which one serves a street decides the figure

DE/Osnabrück.note: three waterworks: Thiene 7.3 dH, Wittefeld 9.6, Düstrup about 13; which one serves a district decides the figure

DE/Pforzheim.note: 6 dH in the southwest, 9 dH elsewhere; treatment brought the hardness down from about 14 dH

DE/Potsdam.note: mostly hard: the Wildpark works at 20-22 dH supplies the west and centre; only the Ferch works delivers medium water

DE/Reutlingen.note: two thirds Lake Constance water at 9.1 dH, the rest from own springs running to about 16 dH; the utility looks the figure up per street

DE/Rostock.note: 2.54 mmol/L at the Rostock waterworks outlet

DE/Saarbrücken.note: four sources between 5.9 and 12.4 dH, blended differently across the network; the utility answers per street

DE/Siegen.note: ninety percent reservoir water from the Obernau and Breitenbach dams

DE/Solingen.note: Sengbach reservoir water treated at Glüder; the published span across plants is 5.2-6.1 dH

DE/Stuttgart.note: 9.0 dH Lake Constance water, 13.0 dH from the Landeswasserversorgung, depending on district

DE/Trier.note: soft Riveris reservoir water from the Irsch works at 4.7 dH supplies most of the city; Kylltal well water measures 9.3 dH

DE/Ulm.note: four zones between 12.7 and 19.1 dH; the city centre drinks Rote Wand well water at the soft end of that span

DE/Wiesbaden.note: four sources spanning almost the whole scale: Taunus tunnel water at 1.7 dH, Naurod 7.2, Schierstein 16.4, Hessisches Ried 19.2; WLW runs a street-level lookup, and its site being offline is why the source link points at the archived copy

DE/Wolfsburg.note: Harz reservoir water blended with groundwater from the Westerbeck and Rühen works

DE/Würzburg.note: the hardest city water in this collection, from the Muschelkalk: Zellingen 25.4 dH, Versbach 38.2, Galgenberg 40.4, Grombühl 42.7
